gamma_cross_gamma_matrix.text: `charm_delta_decay` (Charm Delta Decay) asks how an option's delta changes as time to maturity moves, for a single option described by `spot`, `strike`, `rate`, `sigma`, `tau`, `option_type` and `div_yield`. `gamma_cross_gamma_matrix` asks a different question: how a portfolio's value responds to joint moves in several underlyings. It assembles a symmetric matrix with each underlying's net gamma on the diagonal and cross-gammas off the diagonal, built from the `own_gammas` and `cross_gammas` you supply. That matrix feeds a gamma P&L of 0.5 · ds' G ds for a shock vector ds. In short, charm is about delta over time for one option, while the matrix is about second-order price sensitivity across a portfolio. Note that `charm_delta_decay` uses the time-to-maturity sign convention, which is the opposite of the calendar-time charm often quoted elsewhere.

explain.text: `charm_delta_decay` (Charm Delta Decay) calculates charm, which is how much an option's delta changes as time to maturity changes. You give it `spot`, `strike`, `rate`, `sigma` and `tau`, and optionally `option_type` (call by default) and `div_yield`. It works in the time-to-maturity convention, so it returns +∂Δ/∂τ, and a finite difference of delta with respect to `tau` should reproduce its value. That is the opposite sign from the calendar-time charm (−∂Δ/∂t) often quoted on trading desks and in textbooks. Check which convention any comparison source uses.

when.text:
`charm_delta_decay` (Charm Delta Decay) fits when you need to see how an option's delta shifts as time to maturity changes.

- You're checking how a delta hedge may drift as expiry approaches, using `tau` as the time input.
- You want a value consistent with a finite difference of delta with respect to time to maturity.
- You're comparing against another source: this uses the +∂Δ/∂τ sign, opposite to the calendar-time convention (−∂Δ/∂t) common on desks, so confirm which convention your comparison uses.
- You have a call or put, with an optional `div_yield`, and want the dividend effect included.
- For calendar time decay of option value rather than delta, `theta_time_decay` is listed as Black-Scholes Theta, calendar time decay per year.
